summary: Safety evaluation report for Gemini Robotics 2 (mainly the ER 2 embodied reasoning agent). It introduces the ASIMOV-Agentic benchmark for physical and semantic robot safety: constraint-following refusal, human-proximity stopping, safety tool calling, VLA feasibility awareness, instruction ambiguity and scene uncertainty. It also reports real-world safe-stopping tests on the Apptronik Apollo2 humanoid. It does not use a frontier safety framework and does not cover misuse or catastrophic-risk domains.

framework.name: none
framework.quote: this report focuses primarily on the high-level semantic reasoning and orchestration capabilities of the Agent.

evals: ASIMOV-Agentic 2.1 Unsafe Task Refusal and Safety Constraint Following (Text, Pointing, Bounding Box, Tool-use modalities)

metrics.name: Text-modality safety classification accuracy (all frontier models)

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Embodied unsafe-task refusal under physical and application constraints is reliable in text form, but accuracy varies more across models when grounded into spatial predictions or tool calls.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: This suggests a gap between semantically understanding a constraint (Text) and physically acting on it (Tool Use, Spatial).

evals: ASIMOV-Agentic 2.5 instruction ambiguity (clarification vs fulfilment rates)
over_refusal.finding: Shows a helpfulness-safety tradeoff: models tuned to express uncertainty over-request human help on unambiguous instructions, and low-FNR stop policies cause unnecessary stops.
over_refusal.quote: Conversely, systems tuned to express uncertainty may over-request human help even when provided with unambiguous instructions.

evals: 'attention jailbreaking' planned for future benchmark versions
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Robustness of safety-message attention to attention jailbreaking is named as future work only.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: Future versions of our benchmark will test whether this robustness holds with increasing context length and “attention jailbreaking” [10]

evals: ASIMOV-Agentic 2.6 Obfuscated Instrument Reading (readable-adversarial vs unreadable gauges)
honesty_hallucination.finding: Frontier models tend to verbalize uncertainty rather than hallucinate readings on unreadable instruments, trading off some helpfulness.
honesty_hallucination.quote: Encouragingly, from a safety standpoint, frontier models do seem to prioritize hallucination avoidance in unreadable or hard to read images.

bias_fairness.finding: Explicitly out of scope; fairness is described as ongoing research.
bias_fairness.quote: The benchmark above is designed strictly for physical safety  \( [8, 9] \)  and does not currently encompass privacy and fairness considerations.

privacy.finding: Explicitly out of scope; data minimization is described as ongoing research.
privacy.quote: The benchmark above is designed strictly for physical safety  \( [8, 9] \)  and does not currently encompass privacy and fairness considerations.

evals: Humanoid safe stopping on Apptronik Apollo2 (real-world lab)
Safety Tool Calling (robot_stop on safety messages)

metrics.name: Reliability transitioning to safe pose (VLA, lab)
Safety tool calling accuracy (ER2, Claude Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5)

system_safeguards.finding: ER 2 reliably triggers safe stops; the authors recommend pairing model perception with deterministic low-level guardrails and do not evaluate functional safety hardware.
system_safeguards.quote: This variance indicates that while frontier models offer robust perception capabilities, it is currently best to utilize them alongside deterministic, low-level safety guardrails.

evals: ASIMOV-Agentic benchmark (new, released on Hugging Face)
Proactive Human Safety Monitoring (stereo distance estimation; single-frame and agentic)
VLA Feasibility Awareness (one-step; ToolEmu-inspired confidence-emulator multi-step)

metrics.name: Agentic stop tradeoff
metrics.value: FPR<5% implies FNR>40%; FNR 10-15% implies 15-25% unnecessary stops

other_safety.finding: Embodied, physical-safety benchmark of an agent orchestrating a VLA. No model achieves near-zero false negatives and false positives on human-proximity stopping, and long-horizon confidence-aware planning often fails.
other_safety.quote: Crucially, no model currently operates in the ideal top-right quadrant (near-zero FNR and FPR).

notable_new_eval_methods: ASIMOV-Agentic: Agentic Safety and Uncertainty Resolution Benchmark, publicly released (p.1)
Gemini-based VLA confidence emulator for closed-loop agentic safety evals, ToolEmu-inspired (p.7)
Sensorized human-approach stereo dataset for proximity stop evaluation (p.4)

self_reported_limitations.text: Does not evaluate the underlying functional safety architecture (certified hardware, redundancy, real-time guarantees).
Benchmark covers physical safety only, not privacy and fairness.
Safety tool-calling robustness to longer contexts and attention jailbreaking is not yet tested.
Frontier models' human-proximity stop decisions have unacceptable FNR/FPR tradeoffs; deterministic guardrails still needed.

notes: Comparisons against other frontier models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5) appear mostly in figures. Most numeric results are figure-only. Benchmark datasets were partly synthetically generated with Gemini Pro and Nano Banana.
